collection: NERDC Primary 4 Basic Digital Literacy interface and content creation
note: Original written and device-performance practice from exact-class revised curriculum. Seven practical tasks require preparation and observation. Written precursors do not demonstrate full practical competencies. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.learningObjective: Explain the meaning of interface customisation.
questions.prompt: A pupil chooses a different wallpaper on the classroom tablet. Explain what interface customisation means and how this is an example.
questions.answer: Interface customisation changes the appearance or arrangement of the controls and display used to interact with a device. Choosing a wallpaper changes the background appearance.
questions.explanation: The example concerns a setting of the device interface.

markingGuide.description: Explains customisation as adjusting the interface’s appearance or arrangement.
Connects wallpaper choice to the display background.

questions.deliveryNote: Written understanding or planning precursor. This task alone does not demonstrate device operation or named-application performance.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.prompt: Ada changes her computer’s theme. Musa adds a new sentence to a story in Word. Which action is an example of interface customisation? Explain the difference.
questions.answer: Ada’s theme change is interface customisation. Musa changes the contents of a document.
questions.explanation: The task distinguishes display settings from information created inside an application.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the theme change as interface customisation.
Distinguishes the story edit as a content change.

questions.deliveryNote: Written understanding or planning precursor. This task alone does not demonstrate device operation or named-application performance.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.learningObjective: Change a device theme and wallpaper.
questions.prompt: Practical task. On a teacher-approved practice device, choose one of the installed themes and a teacher-approved wallpaper. Apply both choices and show your teacher what changed. Then restore the starting appearance recorded by your teacher.
questions.answer: The pupil applies the selected theme and wallpaper, identifies the visible changes and restores the recorded starting appearance.
questions.explanation: Assess the changes on the actual device. Menu names and available choices vary.

markingGuide.description: Applies an available installed theme.
Applies the approved wallpaper and identifies its effect.
Restores the teacher-recorded starting appearance.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS Word
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple document using MS Word.
questions.prompt: Practical task in MS Word. Create a short notice for a class reading afternoon. Include the heading Reading Afternoon, the day Friday, the time 2 p.m. and the place Class Library. Arrange it so readers can find each detail easily, and save it in the teacher’s practice folder.
questions.answer: A saved Word document contains the heading and all three event details in a readable arrangement.
questions.explanation: The task assesses the pupil’s ability to create and organise simple digital text.

markingGuide.description: Creates the notice in MS Word.
Includes the heading, day, time and place accurately.
Uses a readable arrangement and saves the document in the assigned folder.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS Word
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple document using MS Word.
questions.prompt: Practical task in MS Word. Your teacher has prepared this sentence in a document: Our class has a red box for paper. Change red to blue and add a second sentence saying where the box is kept. Keep the rest of the original sentence, save the file and show the edited text.
questions.answer: The original sentence now says blue, and a second sentence gives a plausible location for the box.
questions.explanation: Observe editing of the prepared text and the saved result. Accept different clear location sentences.

markingGuide.description: Replaces red with blue while preserving the rest of the sentence.
Adds a meaningful sentence about location.
Saves and shows the edited document.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS Word
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple document using MS Word.
questions.prompt: A pupil is making a Word notice for a school exhibition. The text looks neat, but it does not say where the exhibition will take place. Recommend one edit and explain why it matters to readers.
questions.answer: Add the exhibition’s location. Readers need the place to know where to go.
questions.explanation: This written precursor assesses a purposeful editing decision. Practical Word use must be observed separately.

markingGuide.description: Proposes adding the missing location.
Explains how the addition helps the intended readers.

questions.deliveryNote: Written understanding or planning precursor. This task alone does not demonstrate device operation or named-application performance.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS PowerPoint
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple presentation using MS PowerPoint.
questions.prompt: Practical task in MS PowerPoint. Make a two-slide presentation about looking after a class plant. Put the title Our Class Plant on the first slide. Give two simple care actions on the second slide. Save it, then show both slides to your teacher.
questions.answer: A saved PowerPoint file has a title slide and a second slide with two sensible plant-care actions.
questions.explanation: The focus is creating and displaying simple presentation content. Accept reasonable age-appropriate care actions.

markingGuide.description: Creates the two slides in MS PowerPoint.
Places the title and two actions on the requested slides.
Saves the presentation and shows both slides.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS PowerPoint
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple presentation using MS PowerPoint.
questions.prompt: Practical task in MS PowerPoint. Your teacher has prepared three slides about making a paper card. Their titles, in order, are Decorate the Card, Fold the Paper and Give the Card. Reorder them so the actions make sense. Add the heading Card-Making Steps to the first slide without removing its existing content, then save the presentation.
questions.answer: The slides are ordered Fold the Paper, Decorate the Card and Give the Card. The first slide also carries the added heading.
questions.explanation: Observe that the pupil changes slide order and edits text in the presentation.

markingGuide.description: Reorders the three slides into a sensible sequence.
Adds the heading while preserving the first slide’s existing content.
Saves the edited presentation.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS PowerPoint
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple presentation using MS PowerPoint.
questions.prompt: A pupil’s PowerPoint slide for younger children has a long paragraph describing a three-step activity. Suggest an edit that would help the children follow the steps, and explain how it helps.
questions.answer: Separate the activity into three short, clearly ordered points or slides. This makes each step easier to find and follow.
questions.explanation: Accept different edits that make the sequence clear. This written task is a precursor to observing PowerPoint editing.

markingGuide.description: Suggests separating or shortening the three steps in a clear order.
Explains the benefit for the younger audience.

questions.deliveryNote: Written understanding or planning precursor. This task alone does not demonstrate device operation or named-application performance.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS Excel
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple spreadsheet using MS Excel.
questions.prompt: Practical task in MS Excel. Create a sheet with the headings Item and Number. Enter Pencils with 12, Rulers with 5 and Erasers with 8 on separate rows. Save the sheet and show that each number is beside the correct item.
questions.answer: A saved Excel sheet has two labelled columns and three correctly paired item-and-number rows.
questions.explanation: The task assesses basic entry and organisation in a spreadsheet, without requiring formulas.

markingGuide.description: Creates the two column headings in MS Excel.
Enters all three item-and-number pairs in separate rows.
Saves the sheet and shows the correct row pairings.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS Excel
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple spreadsheet using MS Excel.
questions.prompt: Practical task in MS Excel. Your teacher has prepared a table with Book A and 4 on one row, and Book B and 7 on another. The class now has 6 copies of Book A. Update only its number. Add Book C and 3 on a new row, save the sheet and show your teacher what changed.
questions.answer: The table shows Book A with 6, Book B with 7, and Book C with 3.
questions.explanation: Observe accurate editing of a prepared spreadsheet and preservation of the row that did not need a change.

markingGuide.description: Updates Book A’s number to 6.
Adds Book C with 3 while retaining Book B with 7.
Saves and displays the revised table.

questions.deliveryNote: Teacher prepares the named content and an authorised practice device with the named application or supported display settings. Observe the pupil and the saved result. Application/device availability and actual delivery are unverified.

questions.subject: Basic Digital Literacy
questions.subtopic: Creating and editing with MS Excel
questions.learningObjective: Create and edit a simple spreadsheet using MS Excel.
questions.prompt: An Excel sheet has a column of item names and another column of numbers. A pupil enters a new item name on one row but places its number on the row below. Explain the problem and recommend an edit.
questions.answer: The number no longer lines up with the item it describes. Put the number on the same row as that item and check the other rows for correct pairings.
questions.explanation: This written precursor assesses the organisation of information in a spreadsheet. It does not establish practical Excel performance.

markingGuide.description: Explains that the row mismatch makes the item-and-number relationship unclear.
Recommends correcting the row alignment.

questions.deliveryNote: Written understanding or planning precursor. This task alone does not demonstrate device operation or named-application performance.
